title: Envisioning the future of health technology
author: Envisioning
frame: Radial wheel in six sectors (Regeneration, Treatments, Biogerontology, Telemedicine, Diagnostics, Augmentation) around a central hub. Three concentric bands run outward from the hub, each labelled with its outer year: 2020, 2030, 2040. There is no start-year label; the hub is the poster's present (September 2012). A dot is read as the year of the ring that closes its band (inner band = 2020, middle = 2030, outer = 2040), the same 'between two lines read as the later year' rule as the 2012 technology poster. A dot centred on a ring (overlapping it) is read as that ring's year and marked low confidence. Radial position inside a band is not calibrated (band widths are not proportional to years), so only the band is captured; the note gives the position inside the band.
quote: This visualization is an exercise in speculating about which individual technologies are likely to affect the scenario of health in the coming decades. Arranged in six broad areas, the forecast covers a multitude of research and developments that are likely to disrupt the future of healthcare.

entries.label: Synthetic blood
entries.claim: Synthetic blood starts to affect health care around 2020
entries.note: Dot sits in the inner third of the 2012-2020 (inner) band, clear of the year rings; read as 2020.
entries.interpretation: Manufactured or lab-grown blood substitutes usable for transfusion.

notes: Poster footer reads 'Updated: September 2012'; the PDF was created 2012-09-11 and the PNG was first archived 2012-09-12. Licence CC BY-SA. Read from the archived 2200x2600 PNG (full resolution) with the vector PDF's text layer for exact label positions; dot centres detected by pixel analysis and checked on full-resolution tiles. Ring radii measured on the image: hub edge about 190px, 2020 ring 507px, 2030 ring 721px, 2040 ring (outer edge) 891px, centre at (1097, 1400). Only the 55 white dots are captured. Eleven cluster icons (Synthetic & artificial organs, 3D printers, Life extension, Cryonics, Remote virtual presence, mHealth, Big data, Sensors with Internal/External branches, Neuroprosthetics cluster, Sensory augmentation) are tree roots that group the dots; they sit on fixed radii near the outer edge and are not read as time placements, though the poster's web page lists them among 'Technologies mentioned' (66 names in total). The Neuroprosthetics dot (entry 051) is a separate placement from the Neuroprosthetics cluster icon. The poster never says 'mainstream': its own framing is technologies 'likely to affect' or 'disrupt' healthcare in the coming decades, and the band labels give no start year. The claim wording follows the house template for comparability; graders should treat a placement as 'has a material effect on health care by about the placed year', and should note several labels are speculative end-states (full brain simulation, reverse cryonics, suspended animation) rather than adoption milestones. Five placements sit on a year ring and are low confidence; three of them (Artificial limbs, Reverse cryonics, Telemetrics) would move one decade later under the strict band rule. Two dots (Data-driven diagnostics, Data-driven patient communities) are drawn in the Diagnostics sector but listed under Telemedicine on the web page; category follows the poster.
